title: CrashAgent: Crash Scenario Generation via Multi-modal Reasoning

control_signal.value: Real-world NHTSA crash reports (text description plus sketch diagram) are the input that determines road layout and the behaviors of ego and other road users.

control_mechanism.value: Multi-agent VLM/LLM pipeline: Sketch Agent (visual tree-of-thought prompting with voting), Road Agent (OpenDRIVE via toolbox), Scenario Agent (OpenSCENARIO script via behavior toolbox with parameters).

base_model.value: Prompted pretrained VLMs/LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-flash, Claude 3.7 compared) with tool integration; no trained generative model described.

datasets.value: 150 random samples of NHTSA crash reports, plus 100 synthetic road layouts (22 single roads, 78 intersections) with dense-pattern hard variants.

metrics.value: Lane and road count accuracy and errors (Acc, Err_lane, Err_#road, Err_sum), collision rate, accuracy of road-user count and initial relative position; diversity and realism are claimed.

controllability_evidence.value: Scenario Agent raises collision rate from 0.08 to 0.92 versus a plain VLM on 50 NHTSA samples; Road Agent raises layout accuracy from 0.407 to 0.495.

stated_limitations.value: Depends on quality and coverage of crash reports, biased toward certain accident types; simulator assumptions can cause intended and executed behaviors to differ; VLM hallucination and implausible outcomes in complex scenes.

notes: Reconstructs crashes from reports rather than steering a learned generator; control is via the input report.
